Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-2-prompt-long-0103", "row_sha256": "471b365809f9ec573546b33258982cb8ea721ec810980ed7ac30676c8719bad0", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "can you turn this into a clear prompt for writing an email, not write the email itself yet? i need to contact Harbor Street Music Room about a lesson and there are a few details in the wrong order. the email should sound friendly and straightforward, not stiff, and it should be brief enough that Mira can scan it. Mira Patel is the booking coordinator; we have already spoken once by phone. i’m Nadia Chen, an adult beginner, and i want to ask about a violin lesson. Please keep it as a request, because nothing is booked at this point.

the date i’m hoping for is Thursday, October 17, at 6:10 p.m. i’m looking for a 50-minute, in-person lesson with Jo Alvarez, in Studio 2. those pieces go together; i don’t mean 50 minutes including arrival or a remote lesson. Studio 2 matters because it is quieter than the front room and has a music stand. i’d like to get that particular time, not have the email quietly replace it with some other slot. the date and time are my preference, though, not something Mira has confirmed.

there’s one condition before the email can ask Mira to book anything. Jo has to confirm that she can teach then, and Studio 2 has to be available for the whole 50 minutes starting at 6:10. both things need to be true. Mira told me, “I can keep Studio 2 aside until Friday, but Jo still needs to confirm.” i don’t want the prompt to turn that into confirmation, because the quote only says the room can be held and the teacher still has to confirm. If both the teacher and room are available, ask Mira to book the requested lesson. Don’t say it has already been booked or that the room is definitely reserved.

if either part of that condition doesn’t hold, i want a different, useful next step, not an attempt to book some substitute time. Ask Mira to send me the next two weekday evening start times after 5:30 when Jo and a lesson room are both available. That gives me options to consider without pretending i have chosen one. The fallback is only for the case where the requested time and room cannot both be confirmed; it is not the main request. No need to ask her to hold either alternative.

some background that could help the email feel like a real first lesson: i’m an adult, i played piano for a few years as a child, and i have never had a violin lesson. i can bring a borrowed full-size violin and my shoulder rest. i’d like the first session to work on a comfortable bow hold, getting a steady tone from the open strings, and starting the first line of “Ode to Joy.” those are goals for the lesson, not a demand that Jo cover all of them in a particular order. Don’t make it sound like i’m preparing for a performance or already know how to play.

this would be my first visit to Harbor Street Music Room, so the address and entrance detail might be useful if Mira replies with practical information: it’s 18 Harbor Street, and the entrance is the side door beside the blue mural. i can arrive ten minutes early. i also want to ask whether a new-student form needs to be completed before the lesson, whether the requested time works or not. That question should stay separate from the booking condition; getting a form is not a reason to claim the lesson is confirmed.

for the email, use a subject line and address Mira by name. say i’m Nadia Chen, and make clear i’m asking about a 50-minute in-person beginner violin lesson with Jo, rather than asking for general music information. Please don’t introduce a price, package, discount, payment method, cancellation policy, or another teacher, since i haven’t provided anything about those. I have not paid a deposit and do not want the email to authorize a charge or imply that i have agreed to one.

maybe the request can be organized so that the booking condition and what to do if it fails are easy to distinguish. the quote from Mira can be included as context if it helps explain why i’m checking, but don’t present her words as a booking confirmation. The email should not be so long that it reads like a full biography; include only the background that helps identify the lesson and first-visit question. Keep the two possible outcomes clear and don’t make them sound as if both are being requested at once.

please make the final prompt ask for only the finished email, including its subject line, with no explanation before or after it. It should tell the email writer to ask for the specific booking only if Jo and Studio 2 are both available for the full requested session, and otherwise ask for the two weekday-evening options instead. Keep the fact that no booking is confirmed, and leave the email as a polite inquiry rather than an announcement.", "output": "Write a brief, friendly email to Mira Patel, the booking coordinator at Harbor Street Music Room, from Nadia Chen. Include a subject line, address Mira by name, and make the email a polite inquiry rather than an announcement. No lesson has been booked or confirmed.

Nadia is an adult beginner seeking a 50-minute, in-person violin lesson with Jo Alvarez on Thursday, October 17, at 6:10 p.m. The requested lesson would be in Studio 2. Keep the date, start time, duration, instructor, instrument, and in-person format together; do not substitute another time in the primary request. Studio 2 is preferred because it is quieter than the front room and has a music stand. The requested time is not yet confirmed.

The booking request is conditional: ask Mira to book this specific lesson only if Jo confirms she can teach then and Studio 2 is available for the entire 50 minutes starting at 6:10. Both conditions must hold. Mira previously said, “I can keep Studio 2 aside until Friday, but Jo still needs to confirm.” This means the room may be held, but Jo’s availability—and therefore the booking—has not been confirmed. Do not state that the lesson is booked or that Studio 2 is definitely reserved.

1. If Jo and Studio 2 are both available for the requested session, ask Mira to book it.
2. If either is unavailable, do not ask to book a substitute time or to hold an alternative. Instead, ask Mira to send the next two weekday evening start times after 5:30 when both Jo and a lesson room are available. Present this as an alternative for Nadia to consider, not as a second booking request.

Nadia has played piano for a few years as a child but has never taken a violin lesson. She can bring a borrowed full-size violin and her shoulder rest. Her goals for the first session are to work on a comfortable bow hold, a steady tone from the open strings, and the first line of “Ode to Joy.” These are goals, not a required order or a guarantee that every topic will be covered. Do not imply that she is preparing for a performance or already knows how to play.

This would be Nadia’s first visit to the music room, at 18 Harbor Street; the entrance is the side door beside the blue mural, and she can arrive ten minutes early. Separately from the conditional booking request, ask whether she needs to complete a new-student form before the lesson. Do not treat that question or its answer as confirmation of a booking.

Keep the email concise and include only useful background. Do not introduce prices, packages, discounts, payment methods, cancellation policies, or another teacher. Nadia has not paid a deposit and does not authorize a charge; do not imply otherwise. Return only the finished email, including its subject line, with no explanation before or after it."}]
